Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: Redeployment of VII Corps to Carentan sector and assessment of strategic importance; vulnerability of Carentan and motivation for offensive to advance south to Coutances-St. Lô highway.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_1: In keeping with the desire of Generals Eisenhower and Montgomery to get the American offensive to the south under way, General Bradley had lost no time in redeploying the VII Corps from Cherbourg. As the Cherbourg operation was ending on the last day of June, Bradley ordered the VII Corps headquarters to move to Carentan immediately to assume responsibility for an area on the left (east) of the VIII Corps.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_2: The new VII Corps sector, between the Prairies Marécageuses de Gorges and the flooded Taute River, covered the shallowest part of the Allied beachhead. Through Carentan passed the only highway linking the U.S. troops in the Cotentin with the Allied forces east of the Taute River. The area was considered the weakest and most sensitive part of the entire First Army front. (Map 4)
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_3: A road center and small seaport, Carentan was extremely vulnerable to German attack. The VII Corps positions, facing southwest toward Périers, were only three and a half miles from the center of Carentan. A German counterattack in mid-June had come to within 500 yards of retaking the town, and German field artillery continued to interdict the town and the highway bridge across the Taute River. The First Army staff did not rule out the possibility that a determined German attack might overrun Carentan, cut the Allied beachhead in two, and deny the Allies lateral communication by land. Advancing the front line south of Carentan would eliminate these dangers and the nuisance of German shelling.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_4: More important than these defensive considerations was the offensive motivation. The VII Corps objective was a portion of the Coutances-St. Lô highway. To reach the objective the corps had to pass through a narrow and well-defined corridor constricted by adjacent marshes. Resembling an isthmus two to three miles wide, the corridor between Carentan and Périers severely limited the amount of strength that corps could bring to bear. Only after reaching the Périers-St. Lô highway would VII Corps have adequate room for deploying its forces, and there, south of the Prairies Marécageuses de Gorges, the VII Corps would be at a juncture with the VIII Corps. Continuing south, the two corps would come abreast at the Coutances-St. Lô highway, the final army objective. Should resistance disintegrate before the final objective was reached, General Bradley could use an armored division that he had in the army reserve to exploit the American success.

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: Planning and command arrangements for VII Corps attack starting 4 July; assignment of 83d Infantry Division initial role and expectations for follow-on divisions (4th and 9th).

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_5: General Bradley had thought of launching the VII Corps attack on 3 July, at the same time the VIII Corps jumped off, but he had decided to help VIII Corps on its first day of operations by giving it temporary control of the VII Corps Artillery. He therefore postponed the VII Corps effort until 4 July, when VII Corps was to regain control of its own artillery support. A battalion of 8-inch howitzers and several battalions of medium artillery from army were to reinforce the fires of the corps pieces.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_6: The VII Corps commander was Maj. Gen. J. Lawton Collins... The first problem that General Collins faced was how to use to best advantage in the constricted corps zone the three infantry divisions available to him. Retaining the 4th and 9th Infantry Divisions... Collins on 2 July took control of the 83d Infantry Division... Directing the 83d to advance a little over two miles to Sainteny... Collins set the stage for committing at least part of another division...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_7: Though General Collins wanted the 83d Division to reach Sainteny in a day, he nevertheless recognized that the width of the Carentan-Périers isthmus might enable comparatively few enemy troops to hold up forces of superior numbers...

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: German defensive dispositions opposing VII Corps in Périers sector; composition and leadership of opposing forces.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_8: The Germans in the Périers sector, comprising part of the right (east) wing of the LXXXIV Corps, were under the local operational control of the headquarters of the 17th SS Panzer Grenadier Division... Attached to it was the separate 6th Parachute Regiment...

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: 83d Infantry Division attack on 4 July; initial failures, heavy casualties, command interventions by Collins and Macon, and limited progress.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_9: Aware of the German units... General Collins... had no alternative to striking the Germans frontally... The 83d Division had arrived in Normandy... The 83d Division commander, Maj. Gen. Robert C. Macon... To gain the greatest shock effect... General Macon decided to commit two regiments abreast...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_10: Mishaps plagued the division from the start... The division moved but a short distance toward Sainteny, 200 yards at most...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_11: Following the action... General Collins in midmorning became impatient... On the division right flank the battalion of the 329th Infantry... had managed to advance about 1,000 yards... the battalion commander ordered a withdrawal...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_12: Impatient over the division's lack of progress... For all the strenuous efforts... the regiments were not ready for a concerted attack until late afternoon...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_13: The terrain and stubborn resistance had soured the Fourth of July celebration... A count of personnel... revealed only 300 men... In its first day of combat the 83d Division had lost almost 1,400 men...

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: Continuation of attack on 5 July; continued slow progress, command pressure, minor gains toward Sainteny, additional casualties.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_14: Although the 83d Division had failed... General Collins... ordered the attack to secure Sainteny to continue on 5 July...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_15: The attack on 5 July began... The division jumped off on schedule. Unfortunately, the attack that morning repeated the unsuccessful pattern...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_16: Restless and impatient... By evening the general was shouting... All seemed in vain... Just before dark the division did succeed in reaching a hamlet half way to Sainteny...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_17: In two days the 83d Division had displayed almost all the weaknesses... Despite its deficiencies, the division had managed by sheer persistence to advance over a mile down the Carentan-Périers road... it had suffered an additional 750 casualties.

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: Shift in responsibility on 6 July; 4th Division assumes control of right flank toward Périers; limited progress and continued pressure on 83d Division.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_18: Although the advance of the 83d still did not permit commitment... General Collins... decided to wait no longer... He ordered General Macon to confine his efforts to the left... Collins then instructed the 4th Division commander...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_19: The 4th Division was an experienced unit... Early on 6 July the 12th Infantry began to relieve the 331st... the regiment met firm resistance...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_20: In the meantime, the enemy maintained heavy fire... inflicting about 700 additional casualties.

Sub-event.Sub-event_summary: Planned air support and attack on 7 July; cancellation due to weather, continued ground efforts, minor gains, signs of improvement in 83d Division, overall limited success; German responses and reserve movements.

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_21: The lack of success during the third day... General Collins... turned to an ally, the IX Tactical Air Command... General Collins now asked for more...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_22: Two events marred the beginning of the attack on 7 July... The second disappointment was a drizzling rain... cancellation of the strong air support...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_23: General Macon attempted to swing his 83d Division gradually southward... As the division endeavored to move forward... The 83d Division captured only seventeen prisoners that day...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_24: The 12th Infantry of General Barton's 4th Division had even less success... As the 4th Division rediscovered the problems... the 83d Division began to show signs of improvement...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_25: The improvement was a bright spot... The VII Corps had failed to move even to Sainteny...
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_26: Unknown to the Americans... The VII Corps attack had thus robbed the German sectors... To meet the need for still more reserves...
